subject: In-country processing scope and evidence for Schrems II / SCCs
messages:
From: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@biocare.fr>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@biocare.fr, dpo@mediwell.de
Date: 2028-07-11T09:17:00+02:00
Subject: Initial: In-country processing / SCCs scope question

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Before we proceed with procurement, our legal and DPO teams need clarity on two points around EU-only processing and Schrems II:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that production inference for our tenant can be restricted to EU-only regions (with no failover outside EU) and that the control plane will not access customer data from outside the EU?
2) For SCCs, we need an evidence bundle showing the technical controls that prevent cross-border transfer (eg. routing policies, VPC controls, KMS location, backup locations) and an operational deletion workflow with retention windows and proof-of-deletion artifacts.

Attached is a short scope doc ("SCCs-request-BioCare.pdf"). Can you confirm which items you can provide out of the list and an estimated timeline for evidence?

Simon
Director of IT Compliance
BioCare France

Attachments:
- SCCs-request-BioCare.pdf (application/pdf, 128KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@biocare.fr>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T11:02:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Initial: In-country processing / SCCs scope question

Hi Simon — really glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front: yes on in-country routing (EU regions only) and yes we can provide an evidence package for SCCs items, but there are trade-offs and some operational constraints to note. See details below and a suggested next step.

Summary of what we can provide quickly:
- Routing & processing: ability to pin inference to specific EU regions (FR, DE, NL). Routing policies prevent automatic failover to non-EU unless manually enabled.
- Control plane: customer data plane is in-customer-region; control plane access can be restricted via allowed-admin IP ranges and requires KMS auth — we can provide attestations and access logs.
- KMS & keys: we support customer-managed keys in EU KMS (BYOK) and HSM-backed options.
- Backups: backups are optional and can be configured to remain in the selected EU region; we will highlight caveats for cross-region snapshots (we can disable).
- Deletion proof: we can produce proof-of-deletion records (logs + checksum) and a deletion runbook.

Open / clarifying items we need from you:
- Does BioCare require hard isolation with NO automated cross-region failover at the account level, or would manual failover be acceptable in an incident?
- Any specific retention windows for logs/backups that differ from our default 90-day policy?

Suggested next step: a 30–45 minute technical sync with our security engineering and your DPO to walk the evidence bundle items. I can host on Thursday morning CEST — Naomi, Jordan, can you join?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@biocare.fr>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T08:45:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Initial: In-country processing / SCCs scope question — evidence checklist

Hi Simon — Naomi from Security here. Following Vanessa's note, I put together an evidence checklist and attached an annotated SCCs draft highlighting where Redwood supplies artifacts. High-level notes:

- Architecture diagrams: we will provide an in-region component diagram showing data paths for inference and control-plane interactions.
- Audit logs: tokenized access logs and admin action logs for the account for the last 90 days (we can extend on request).
- KMS proof: metadata about key residency and HSM attestation statement (if customer BYOK used).
- Backups: manifest of backup locations + policy settings; if you require backups disabled we can set that as a configuration.
- Deletion workflow: runbook + sample proof-of-deletion (S3 object deletion markers + write-once CT log entry).
- SCCs mapping: we map each SCC clause to our artifact types; some SCC obligations (eg. lawful access notice) concern jurisdictional law and we can provide our legal position & prior audit summaries but not change sovereign law risk.

Attached: "SCCs-annotated-draft.pdf" and a small CSV index ("evidence-index.csv") pointing to the Drive folder with samples.

Quick question for scope: Do you need the evidence signed/acknowledged by our legal team (we can provide) or is an engineer-signed attestation acceptable for your procurement review?

Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- SCCs-annotated-draft.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)
- evidence-index.csv (text/csv, 12KB)

From: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@biocare.fr>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@biocare.fr, dpo@mediwell.de
Date: 2028-07-13T10:12:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Initial: In-country processing / SCCs scope question — evidence checklist

Thanks Naomi — that checklist is helpful. A few clarifications from our side after a DPO review:

1) Failover: BioCare requires NO automated cross-border failover for Production workloads. Manual failover by a named admin with documented approvals is acceptable.
2) Logs: we need proof-of-deletion for access logs older than the retention window when requested by us (audit request) — an on-demand deletion evidence process.
3) Legal attestation: for procurement we need a signed legal attestation from Redwood confirming the artifacts map to SCC obligations (engineer-signed is not sufficient).

If you can confirm the two operational changes (disable automated cross-border failover for our tenant; on-demand deletion evidence flow), plus provide a legal-signed attestation, we can move to internal commercial review and sign the SCCs addendum.

Simon

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T16:05:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Initial: In-country processing / SCCs scope question — evidence checklist

Simon — thanks for the clarity. Confirmations and next steps below.

Confirmations (to meet BioCare procurement asks):
- Automated cross-border failover: we will disable automatic non-EU failover for your production tenant. The account-level setting will be locked to EU regions; manual failover requires a documented approval process and will be logged. Estimated delivery: we will apply the configuration and provide the control-plane change log within 2 business days.
- On-demand deletion evidence for logs: we can provide an on-demand proof-of-deletion package (log manifests + deletion markers + signed hash) within 5 business days of a formal request. We will add a short SLA clause in the addendum.
- Legal attestation: our Legal team will produce a signed attestation mapping our artifacts to the SCCs clauses. Jordan, can you coordinate a brief legal-signed attestation and upload to the Drive folder?

Next steps:
1) I'll schedule the 30-minute evidence walkthrough with Naomi and Soojin — proposed slot Thursday 2028-07-18 09:30 CEST.
2) Jordan will draft the legal attestation and upload the DocuSign link (I've attached a DocuSign stub: "docsign-biocare-scope.pdf").
3) After the walkthrough, we'll provision the account-level setting to lock regions and produce the change log + deletion workflow sample.

If that works I will send a calendar invite and a small pre-read (architecture diagram + annotated SCCs link).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- docsign-biocare-scope.pdf (application/pdf, 45KB)
